brief: Deutsche Bank reports the session rather than arguing a thesis, but ties one chain across assets. New attacks on Saudi energy sites, explosions near Kharg Island and the US destruction of five Iranian tankers pushed Brent to $99.34/bbl this morning, near $100 for the first time in six weeks, and lifted the 6-month Brent future 1.52% to $84.78/bbl, which the note reads as growing scepticism that oil reverts over coming months. Higher energy costs fed inflation pricing: European front-end gas rose 3.46% to 75.80 euros per MWh with storage only 67% full against 79% a year earlier, and the 1-year euro inflation swap rose to 3.40%. That backdrop dampened risk appetite, the S&P 500 fell 0.58% with over 70% of the index lower, and US front-end yields rose, the 2-year to 4.39% and the 5-year to a 19-month high of 4.56%. European sovereign yields still fell because real rates dropped even as breakevens rose. China's August producer prices accelerated to +3.8%, above the +3.6% consensus, which the note attributes to the same energy shock while domestic demand stayed subdued.
